features.title: One port for version-control providers
features.summary: Jujutsu and git support plug in the same way, and the best one for a folder is used.
features.details: Providers serve the same dshx API id under their own owner; a caller asks every served provider which claims a path and uses the highest priority one to isolate a thread or snapshot and restore files.
failureModes: A provider whose detect fails is skipped instead of failing the caller.
A path no provider claims resolves to nothing, so the caller keeps the project checkout.

verification.testName: picks the highest-priority provider that claims the path
answers nothing when no provider claims the path or none is loaded
resolves the provider through the Effect service, skipping a provider whose detect fails

features.title: Which VCS owns a path
features.summary: DSH tells whether a folder uses Jujutsu or git from the folder itself.
features.details: VcsDetector (subpath ./detect) names jj or git for a path from the nearest .jj or .git above it, jj first when both exist, reading only the filesystem; jj-integration and diffs-review pick their jj or git adapter with it.
failureModes: A path outside any repository, or one deleted meanwhile, detects nothing and kindOf reads it as jj so callers keep their jj errors.

verification.testName: prefers jj in a colocated checkout, picks git for a git-only one, and reads the nearest marker
reads a folder outside any repository, or one deleted meanwhile, as jj so its errors stay unchanged

telemetry.reason: Pure filesystem existence checks with no process, socket or network; the caller's span covers them.

features.title: Which project a thread belongs to
features.summary: Tells other plugins which project a thread belongs to, counting a thread workspace for the project it was cut from.
features.details: WorkspaceAttribution (subpath ./workspace-attribution) maps a Session to its DSH project from the workspace registry: a thread workspace (<repository>-threads/thread-…, or a provider-reported custom threads directory) belongs to the project it was cut from; a Session no workspace lists falls back to its recorded cwd. thread-sidebar groups by it and agents picks a project's default agent with it.
failureModes: A Session outside every registered project resolves to no project, so the caller keeps its own fallback.

verification.testName: attributes a registered thread workspace session, and one whose thread workspace was forgotten, to the project
uses a reported custom threads directory

telemetry.reason: Pure functions over registry rows the caller passes; no I/O.
